entries.content:
The Tanooki Suit, or Tanooki Costume, is a fairly uncommon item found in Super Mario Bros. 3 and its subsequent remakes in Super Mario All-Stars and Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3 that transforms Mario into Tanooki Mario. It is based on bake-danuki, Japanese mythological creatures inspired by Japanese raccoon dogs (tanuki) who can use leaves to shape-shift and cause chaos. The suit is an add-on to the Raccoon form that allows Mario or Luigi to temporarily turn into a statue and become immune to enemies and obstacles, in addition to flying and attacking enemies with tail swipes. According to Shigeru Miyamoto in the Super Mario Bros. 3 entry of the 25th Anniversary Super Mario History Booklet, he was aware that most players outside Japan would be overall confused with the Tanooki Suit and the transformation, but he left it in because he was too excited to remove it.

Effect:
"Transforms {{user}} or {{char}} into Tanooki {{user}} or {{char}}, granting him the abilities of Raccoon {{user}} or {{char}} as well as allowing him to briefly turn into Statue {{user}} or {{char}}. Statue {{user}} or {{char}} is invulnerable while active"

entries.name: Vanish Cap
entries.content:
The Vanish Cap, or Blue Cap, is a cap found in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS. When worn, the Vanish Cap turns Mario into Vanish Mario for 20 seconds. In this form, Mario can walk through enemies, metal fences, and certain walls. The Vanish Cap music is the same as the Wing Cap music. To use a Vanish Cap, Mario must first press the Vanish Cap Switch in the course Vanish Cap Under the Moat, which activates blue blocks. Vanish Caps appear in Big Boo's Haunt; Dire, Dire Docks; Snowman's Land; Wet-Dry World; and Vanish Cap Under the Moat. In Super Mario 64 DS, Luigi gains the ability to become immaterial when he picks up a Power Flower, but the Vanish Cap itself is absent. In Super Mario Odyssey, a cap similar to the Vanish Cap called the Invisibility Hat is unlocked after the Darker Side of the Moon is completed. Unlike the Vanish Cap, the Invisibility Hat causes Mario to be invisible for an unlimited period of time until he changes to a different cap. The suit is purely for aesthetic effect, so abilities such as walking through mesh walls are not retained while he wears the cap.

Effect:
"Temporarily transforms {{user}} or {{char}} into Vanish {{user}} or {{char}}, granting him intangibility and allowing him to walk through enemies, chain-link fences, ice, and mirrors"

entries.name: Viking Helmet
entries.content:
The Viking helmet (or Viking Helmet), also known as Bull Pot, Bull Hat or simply Bull, is a Power Up Pot that turns Wario into Bull Wario in Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 and Virtual Boy Wario Land. In both games, when Wario grabs the item, a helmet with bull horns appears on his head. In this form, Wario can destroy his enemies and blocks much easier, make a shock wave by crashing into the ground, and stick to the ceiling. The power works differently in Virtual Boy Wario Land, as Wario cannot stick to ceilings, but his Barge speeds up. However, this is one of the heaviest forms, making it hard to jump out of quicksand.

Effect:
"Transforms {{user}} or {{char}} into Bull {{user}} or {{char}}, which allows him to destroy blocks with just one Body Slam instead of two, and is able to do a ground pound that destroys any enemy or block directly hit and creates a shock wave that stuns any nearby enemy. He is also able to stick to the ceiling with his horns"

entries.name: Weird Mushroom
entries.content:
The Weird Mushroom is a power-up in Super Mario Maker and Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS. It is a skinnier, more realistically shaped Super Mushroom. Upon use, Mario turns into Weird Mario, becoming taller and slimmer and gaining the abilities of Luigi, with higher jumps but lower traction. It looks similar to a normal Super Mushroom, but with a short cap and a very thin base. A Super Mushroom cannot override the effect of this mushroom, but the Weird Mushroom can override a Super Mushroom's effect. However, a Fire Flower, Mystery Mushroom, or Big Mushroom can override the Weird Mushroom's effects, while Fire Mario, Costume Mario, and Big Mario are unaffected by Weird Mushrooms. The Weird Mushroom has a 1% chance of spawning wherever a Super Mushroom is placed, except during upload check, where it was changed to never randomly spawn after an update. However, it can also be unlocked by clearing all four of the Nintendo World Championships courses. Upon unlocking the Weird Mushroom, the player can use it by shaking a Super Mushroom in the editor. In Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS, however, the player starts the game with the Weird Mushroom in their item selection. The Weird Mushroom is exclusive to the Super Mario Bros. game style, so if the player changes the game style, every Weird Mushroom object turns back into a Super Mushroom. In Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS, however, the Weird Mushroom is replaced by the Super Leaf in the Super Mario Bros. 3 style, the Cape Feather in the Super Mario World style, and the Propeller Mushroom in the New Super Mario Bros. U style. The Weird Mushroom and its form would have returned in Super Mario Maker 2, but they were scrapped from the final game for unknown reasons.

Effect:
"Transforms {{user}} or {{char}} into Weird {{user}} or {{char}}, a skinnier form of {{user}} or {{char}} with Luigi's physics, including a higher jump and worse traction"

entries.name: Wing
entries.content:
The Wing is an item that appears only in Super Mario Bros. Special. When Mario collects it, he is able to fly through the air using the game's swimming controls. However, the power-up is only temporary, and if the player is not careful, Mario may fall somewhere undesirable once it expires. The item can be found exclusively in World 3-2 and World 4-1, hiding inside a Hidden Block. The Wing functions similarly to the P-Wing that was later introduced in Super Mario Bros. 3.

Effect:
"Temporarily allows {{user}} or {{char}} to fly through the air as if swimming"

entries.name: Wing Cap
entries.content:
The Wing Cap, or Winged Cap, is an item found in Super Mario 64. It is Mario's signature power-up in Super Mario 64, being shown on the game's box art and a majority of its merchandise.

Effect:
"Temporarily transforms {{user}} or {{char}} into Wing {{user}} or {{char}}, allowing him to fly after performing a Triple Jump or being shot from a cannon"

entries.name: Wonder Flower
entries.content:
The Wonder Flower is a flower power-up that first appeared in Super Mario Bros. Wonder.

Effect:
"Activates a Wonder Effect. There are various effects, including making certain pipes move up and down or bend, stretching players and enemies, transforming the player into something different like a Spike Ball, causing hordes of enemies to appear, or spawning flower coins. In Super Mario Run, it activates Coin Rush"

entries.name: Wonder Effects
entries.content:
Wonder Effects:
"Wonder Effects, also referred to as Wonder Powers, are the central mechanic of Super Mario Bros. Wonder, triggered by collecting Wonder Flowers. Collecting them in different levels causes various effects, including making certain pipes move up and down or bend, stretching players and enemies, transforming the player into something different like a Spike Ball, causing hordes of enemies to appear, or spawning flower coins. During a Wonder Effect, a wavy effect is added to the corners of the screen, and a decimal place is added to the flower coin counter as smaller flower coins are scattered throughout the stage, with ten of them adding up to a single coin. The goal of every Wonder Effect is to collect a Wonder Seed, which ends the Wonder Effect. Some Wonder Effects have time limits, and some, like the music-based ones, speed up power-up and power-down animations (the latter also having their sound effect sped up), and remove hitstop like in local multiplayer. A group of voices can be heard exclaiming "Won-der!" as a Wonder Effect begins (with a more electric guitar-like distorted version being heard in Missile Meg Mayhem). During an effect, the background often changes, ? Blocks (and ! Blocks when the "Add ! Blocks" badge is equipped) turn magenta, and all Coins dance to the music"

Example List of Wonder Effects that can happen with the Wonder Flower:
"Causes pipes to gain eyes and start moving up and down, Causes pipes to come to life as Inchworm Pipes, Causes Piranha Plants and their variants to sing and pop in and out of pipes rhythmically, Pipes start moving rhythmically, Summons an endless rain of Super Stars. Collecting one resets a 10-second timer, Summons a stampeding Wonder Bulrush herd, Wonder Hoppos appear, Creates hidden roads for {{user}} or {{char}} and Rolla Koopas to run on, Causes Spikes to dance and throw Spike Balls rhythmically, Gives {{user}} or {{char}} the ability to stretch their body, as well as causing enemies to stretch out similarly (The whole stage may also become silhouetted), Causes {{user}} or {{char}} to float freely in the air, Causes pipes to fall, Causes {{user}} or {{char}} and Wonder Bowser Jr. to shrink or grow, Summons a Wonder Smackerel, The dry and flooded areas are inverted, Causes Wonder Blewbirds to blow rainbow-colored bouncy bubbles instead of arrows, Reveals a giant snowball that begins rolling and destroying the level, A snowstorm begins, creating Snow Blocks everywhere, {{user}} or {{char}} starts walking on the walls from a top-down perspective, Pole Blocks start extending in all sorts of shapes, {{user}} or {{char}} turns into a Puffy Lift, guiding Spike Balls along the way, The flying battleship's figurehead turns alive and begins firing explosive blasts at the player, Creates colorful Dotted-Line Blocks and sets off a timed rhythm sequence, {{user}} or {{char}} starts freefalling, Causes Linking Lifts to grow taller and/or wider, and summons a Lakitu trio to throw coins and Wonder Tokens all over the course, Causes the ground to become icy or sticky, Summons zigzagging bolts of lightning across the screen, Summons Big Hoppycats, Summons Wonder Anglefish, {{user}} or {{char}} transforms into their Hoppycat form, Summons a Wonder Konk, Causes time to speed up, slow down, or both periodically, Causes an ancient temple to rise from below the ground, The whole level tilts, causing Giant Spiked Balls and other objects to roll, Causes "Ninji Disco" to play and Ninjis to dance, Turns {{user}} or {{char}} into their Balloon form, Summons Rift Mario to chase the player, A Wonder Shova pushes a giant Bowser statue towards {{user}} or {{char}}, Causes water to rise into the air like a lava lamp, Summons a swarm of Wonder Gnawshers, Causes Mushroom Platforms to glow and start moving up and down rhythmically, catapulting Jack O'Goomba-themed pumpkins upwards, Starts a quiz and {{user}} or {{char}} must pull on the Taily with the right answer to complete three questions, Summons King Boo to sing and chase {{user}} or {{char}} with Noknoks and Boos singing along, Turns {{user}} or {{char}} into a Wubba, The ground becomes slimy and slippery, Causes Semisolid Platforms to move around, {{user}} or {{char}} turns into a Spike Ball, {{user}} or {{char}} becomes invincible and able to swim through magma, Summons a giant Spike statue in the background that spits fiery boulders at {{user}} or {{char}}, Revives a fossil into an Ancient Dragon, Summons several Wonder Missile Megs, Turns {{user}} or {{char}} into their Metal form, Creates a ship made out of blocks with a cannon, Causes "Bowser's Blazing Beats" to play and Fire Knuckles and platforms and Bill Blasters to move and fire rhythmically"

entries.name: Super Crown (For User)
